name: Mara Adair
tagline: I don’t stop at the deck.
intro: I make campaigns, research tools, and small digital systems that carry the work from the brief to the people using it.
about: I’m Mara, a strategist and independent builder. I’m drawn to projects where a good research finding needs a second life as something people can use: an invitation, a workflow, a clear explanation, or a small piece of software.

My work spans civic campaigns, cultural programs, operations tools, and service proposals. I like sitting in on real handoffs, reading what people ask when they get stuck, and keeping the early versions around so the final decision has a record.
In the Lab I make browser experiments and 3D studies. They let me test ideas about movement, type, and material at a smaller scale than a client project.

experience.title: Campaign strategy lead
experience.summary: Mapped the first-visit journey for public programs, wrote campaign briefs, and worked with designers and hosts to keep the invitation useful through arrival.

experience.title: Independent product designer and developer
experience.summary: Built small tools for coordination and research, from a shift-swap app to a browser extension for keeping excerpts in context.

experience.title: Service research collaborator
experience.summary: Worked with the service team on rider decisions during disruptions and prototyped a status board with a visible, useful offline state.

experience.title: Campaign writer and facilitator
experience.summary: Helped first-time participants picture themselves in a studio workshop and designed a class format built around audience questions.

experience.title: Editorial collaborator
experience.summary: Edited a documentary script for pacing and clarity, keeping narration and interview material distinct during the production handoff.

testimonials.quote: Mara brought the campaign back to the question people were actually asking. We were still using that visitor map when the next program brief came around.
testimonials.author: Dara Bell

testimonials.quote: The useful part was watching her test the swap that went wrong. The team finally had a simple way to tell who was still on the roster.
testimonials.author: Imogen Ames
